public_rationale: In its August 11, 2026 earnings call, CoreWeave reported adding about 500 megawatts of active power during April–June 2026 [e1]. This challenges the negligible-additions premise, but measures power at one provider rather than customer-ready AI compute across major providers [e1]. It does not establish whether slow supply materially exaggerates apparent demand, so the causal claim remains unresolved [e1].
limitations: Active power does not establish installed accelerators, customer-ready compute, or actual utilization.
The evidence lacks comparable capacity additions across major providers and customer-level evidence separating supply constraints from demand growth.
The claim supplies no numerical threshold for negligible additions.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Slow capacity additions create an illusory signal of insatiable AI compute demand; barely any compute is actually coming online.

statement.excerpt: And because capacity is coming on very slowly otherwise, it’s sending out an illusory signal around “insatiable demand” for AI compute, when the actual situation is that barely any compute is coming online, even when it’s built by the largest and best-capitalized companies in the world.

from_speaker: capacity is coming on very slowly
barely any compute is coming online
our_interpretation: Read barely any compute as negligible additions to usable AI computing capacity, not literally zero additions.
Use April–June 2026, the latest completed reporting quarter before the post, to test the ongoing capacity assertion.
Compare additions with the operating fleet and announced delivery schedules without inventing a numerical cutoff.
Read the causal assertion as saying that slow supply materially exaggerates the appearance of broad, sustainable demand.
Keep energized power, installed accelerators, customer-ready compute, and actual utilization separate.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable operational records show negligible usable AI capacity additions across major providers, and customer, utilization, and order evidence shows that slow supply materially explains the apparent strength of demand.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records show substantial usable AI capacity additions across major providers, or show that strong unmet demand persists across diverse customers despite substantial additions. A single provider's power expansion challenges the claim but does not by itself settle the market-wide causal assertion.

evidence.locator: Q&A, Michael Turrin question and following Nitin Agrawal answer
evidence.explanation: The analyst identifies a substantial quarterly power addition, which management confirms in the following answer. This challenges the negligible-additions premise, but active power at one provider does not establish market-wide usable AI compute or the cause of demand.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Comparable April–June 2026 records of customer-ready AI capacity across major providers, measured in consistent compute units and compared with operating fleets and delivery schedules. Utilization, customer concentration, and unmet-order evidence would also need to establish whether slow supply materially exaggerates apparent demand.
